messages:
nina: Follow-up to the RFC: proposing a tiny "claim bridge" service between frontdoor and admission. Purpose: give frontdoor a small, cacheable verdict so it can immediately decide shaping vs route-to-slowpath without owning full quota logic.

raj: Nice. What does the contract look like?

nina: Rough sketch:
```
POST /claims { tenant, req_id, token_est, short_hint }
Resp 200 { verdict: 'ok'|'hold'|'escalate', ttl_ms, advisory_hint?, reasons[] }
```
Simple, keeps numeric limits out of the API initially.

hannah: Important: don't make this a hard single-source write path for abuse signals. We should keep local detectors at edge and let bridge merge local hint + cached central bucket. Central writes only on heavyweight signals.

raj: If the bridge is sync and frontdoor waits, we add latency. If async + cache, correctness suffers. What's our tolerance?

nina: Target: sync p95 < 7ms, p99 < 25ms. If we can't hit that we default to cached async mode with best_effort=true flag and more conservative frontdoor policies.

edge-bot: canary-plan created: cluster=eng-platform, pct=8, ticket=ENGPLAT-1301

hannah: We need staleness semantics. Proposal: bridge returns ttl_ms + staleness_score (0-100). Frontdoor rule: if ttl expired OR staleness_score > 70 then map to 'hold' unless local detector strongly green.

raj: Also add reason codes for observability: e.g., ["burst_limit","central_abuse_high","stale_cache"]. This will help slices in dashboards and playbooks.

nina: Agreed. On interface boundary: avoid numeric tokens/sec unless we commit to tight coupling. Start qualitative with optional advisory_hint like "shaping: 50r/s" for future experiments.

hannah: Rollout steps I suggest:
1) implement bridge behind flag && internal tenants only
2) run synthetic traffic comparison: feed recorded 72h traffic to both legacy and bridge and collect decision divergence metrics
3) canary at 8% with telemetry and kill-switch thresholds (fallback spike >3% for 5m)
4) iterate to async cached mode if latency targets fail

raj: Testing matrix: unit rules, integration with frontdoor when cache cold, chaos test where central bucket writes get delayed, long-run drift test to detect decision skew across regions.

nina: On degraded modes: frontdoor MUST be able to fall back to capacity-based local tokens so we never block traffic because bridge is down. Bridge failure = conservative local default.

edge-bot: Note added: telemetry needs: per-tenant verdict ratio, verdict latency histogram, cache hit ratio, reason-code breakdown. Alert: verdict-latency-p99 > 30ms for 10m -> P1.

hannah: Add SDK header for clients: optional opt-in header x-rw-bridge: verdict=hold|escalate to let SDK show queueing/UX hints. Keep it opt-in so we don't break existing clients.

raj: One more design trade: should bridge accept batched claims? Batching reduces overhead but complicates per-request mapping. Maybe allow batch for high-throughput paths and single claim for latency-sensitive ones.

nina: Good call. Support both but prefer single for first pass. We'll add batch endpoint in v2.

hannah: Owners: nina=design+impl, raj=frontdoor integration, hannah=telemetry+runbook. I'll draft a follow-up note with required metrics and kill-switch numbers.

deploy-bot: task ENGPLAT-1301 created and assigned to nina, due in 10 days.

nina: Thanks. I'll post the small RFC addendum with explicit API shape and the canary checklist later today.
